name: Laid on a sand bed, sand-jointed
process: Exterior stone paving laid flexibly: the ground is excavated and compacted, a densely graded crushed-stone sub-base is laid, then a bedding course of sharp limestone screenings (or concrete sand) about 38 mm deep, levelled and tamped. The stones are laid course by course and brought to level with mallets, the surface is tamped through a board, and sand is broomed and tamped into the joints so each stone is fully bedded round its perimeter.

photograph: Joints about a centimetre wide, filled nearly flush with pale sand that darkens when damp and stays damp longer than the stone.
Slight lippage between stones; sand washed low in some joints after rain.
Over years the joints fill with fines and organic matter and green with moss (history paving.joint-infill).
